sources.citation: GenStart "Honda EU7000is Standard 2 Wire Start System Manual", https://genstart.ca/uploads/3/4/9/7/34974774/manual_eu7000is_standard.pdf (7 pp) and older revision (GS7000is2WS module) https://genstart.ca/uploads/3/4/9/7/34974774/manual_standard.pdf (6 pp); AutoStart harness sheet https://genstart.ca/uploads/3/4/9/7/34974774/manual_autostart_harness.pdf (checked: 2026-09-01)

transport: 2-wire maintained dry contact (black/white of the 6 ft Control Harness) · open-circuit voltage: ? · closed-contact current: ? · polarity: none stated; module power red/black to battery (p6) · fusing: **the two revisions disagree** — older: "internal contacts are rated for 30 amps and are NOT fused. Circuit protection is required" (p6, repeated on the AutoStart harness sheet); newer: "The control circuit is protected by the GenStart system 5A main fuse" (p7) · ignition-switch position: **not stated** in the Standard manual · temperature: not in the manual (the -40 °C figure appears only on the store page) · fob: none in Standard.

models.name: Honda EU7000is (EU7000isN)
models.rating: 5.5 kVA rated / 7.0 kVA max, gasoline (EFI), electric start yes (12 V 11.2 Ah)

gotchas: Module goes in-line with **both** the Honda ignition-switch and start-switch connectors behind the control panel (steps 7–8, p4–5) — it does not use Honda's factory remote coupler.
"Touch the two wires ... together and the generator will start. Disconnect the wires and the generator will stop" (p7). No crank time, retry or run-feedback documented.

Premium wireless variant, https://genstart.ca/uploads/3/4/9/7/34974774/manual_eu7000is_premium_wireless.pdf: "It is NOT necessary to have the generator ignition switch on for the wireless start" and "The 2-wire start remains active when [wireless system] switch is off" (p9). Fob-vs-contact precedence: not stated.
A 30 A unfused contact rating vs a 5 A fuse is the kind of disagreement to settle on the bench before sizing our series relays.
